close_reason: Introduced CalendarSetParams and TaskListSetParams; reshaped calendar_set/task_list_set to take params: Option<XxxSetParams> matching mail-canonical mailbox_set/address_book_set/filenode_set shape. Threaded params.extra onto wire via entry().or_insert() (typed wins on collision). calendar_set keeps if_in_state as inline Option<&State> per email_submission_set canonical (the bead body's suggestion to bundle if_in_state was inconsistent with the workspace canonical; followed the canonical instead). Added serde as direct dep of jmap-tasks-client (see ops7.13 for the broader divergence). 18 test-result lines green, full workspace clippy + rustdoc + fmt clean. Commit a017846.
description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:139 (`MailboxSetParams { on_destroy_remove_emails: Option<bool> }`)
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mailbox.rs:116, :156 (`mailbox_set(params: Option<MailboxSetParams>)`, applied via `if let Some(v) = p.on_destroy_remove_emails`)
- crate-jmap-contacts-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40 (`AddressBookSetParams { on_destroy_remove_contents: Option<bool> }`)
- crate-jmap-contacts-client/src/methods/addressbook.rs:180 (`if let Some(v) = p.on_destroy_remove_contents`)
- crate-jmap-filenode-client/src/methods/filenode.rs:80 (`FileNodeSetParams { on_destroy_remove_children: Option<bool>, ... }`) — `filenode_set` uses the struct
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:116 (`calendar_set(on_destroy_remove_events: Option<bool>, if_in_state: Option<&State>)`) — **inline, no Params struct**
- crate-jmap-tasks-client (cargo find: `task_list_set(on_destroy_remove_tasks: Option<bool>)`) — **inline, no Params struct**

**Divergence**:

All five extension `_set` methods that have a "cascade on destroy" knob serialize the same JSON key shape (`onDestroyRemove<Children>`, `onDestroyRemoveEmails`, etc.) but expose it through two different API shapes:

| Crate | Method | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| mail | `mailbox_set` | `params: Option<MailboxSetParams>` (struct holds `on_destroy_remove_emails`) |
| contacts | `address_book_set` | `params: Option<AddressBookSetParams>` (struct holds `on_destroy_remove_contents`) |
| filenode | `filenode_set` | `params: Option<FileNodeSetParams>` (struct holds `on_destroy_remove_children`) |
| calendars | `calendar_set` | `on_destroy_remove_events: Option<bool>` inline (also `if_in_state` inline) |
| tasks | `task_list_set` | `on_destroy_remove_tasks: Option<bool>` inline |

**What goes wrong**:

1. A consumer writing JMAP client code that touches multiple object types must remember which crate exposes the cascade flag inline vs in a Params struct. Two crates (calendars, tasks) disagree with three siblings (mail, contacts, filenode).
2. The Params shape is the canonical-template shape (mail-client is canonical per workspace AGENTS.md). When future extension authors mirror the mail-client pattern they will see 3 of 5 followers and reasonably conclude Params is the convention — only to find calendars and tasks have not joined.
3. The Params shape is more forward-compatible: a future RFC field added to `<Object>/set` arguments goes onto the struct without changing the method signature. The inline shape requires a method signature change (breaking) every time the RFC adds a knob.
4. The mail-client and contacts-client docs at line 116/180 use `if let Some(v) = p.on_destroy_remove_*` as the application idiom; calendars/tasks use `if let Some(odre) = on_destroy_remove_events`. Side-by-side they look like different protocols.

**Fix**: introduce `CalendarSetParams { on_destroy_remove_events, if_in_state }` and `TaskListSetParams { on_destroy_remove_tasks }`, and switch the two methods to `params: Option<XxxSetParams>`. Matches mail-canonical-template. Pre-1.0 v0.1.x — small breaking change for the two outliers.

Alternative (rejected): inline everywhere. That would force breaking changes on mail/contacts/filenode for the same workspace-API consistency, AND lose the forward-compat property described in (3).
title: calendars/tasks `_set` take `on_destroy_remove_*` inline; mail/contacts/filenode wrap it in a `*SetParams` struct — same RFC 8620 §5.3 cascade-on-destroy semantics, two API shapes
